title: Ezekiel Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 16.

questions.question: Who was Jerusalem's father according to Ezekiel 16?
questions.correctAnswer: An Amorite
questions.explanation: Jerusalem's father was an Amorite as stated in Ezekiel 16:3.

questions.question: What was NOT done for Jerusalem on the day she was born?
questions.correctAnswer: She was crowned
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:4 lists that her navel was not cut, she was not washed in water, nor salted, nor swaddled, but it does not say she was crowned on the day she was born.

questions.question: True or False: None pitied Jerusalem when she was cast out in the open field.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:5 confirms that none pitied Jerusalem when she was cast out in the open field on the day she was born.

questions.question: What did the LORD say when He saw Jerusalem polluted in her own blood?
questions.correctAnswer: Live
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 16:6, the LORD said to Jerusalem 'Live' when He saw her polluted in her own blood.

questions.question: How did Jerusalem prosper after being caused to multiply by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Became a kingdom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:13 states Jerusalem prospered into a kingdom after being adorned and increased in beauty.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD entered into a covenant with Jerusalem and made her His.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:8 records that the LORD swore and entered into a covenant with Jerusalem, and she became His.

questions.question: What did the LORD do to Jerusalem after entering into a covenant with her?
options: Washed her with water and anointed her with oil
questions.correctAnswer: Washed her with water and anointed her with oil
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:9 says the LORD washed Jerusalem thoroughly and anointed her with oil.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT given to Jerusalem as adornment by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold rings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:10-12 mentions broidered work, badgers' skin, fine linen, silk, bracelets, chains, jewels, earrings, and a crown, but not gold rings specifically.

questions.question: True or False: Jerusalem’s beauty and renown went forth among the heathen because of her own doing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:14 states that Jerusalem's renown went forth among the heathen for her beauty because of the comeliness the LORD put upon her, not her own doing.

questions.question: What did Jerusalem do because she trusted in her own beauty?
options: Played the harlot and poured out fornications
questions.correctAnswer: Played the harlot and poured out fornications
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:15 states Jerusalem trusted in her own beauty and played the harlot, pouring out fornications on every one that passed by.

questions.question: What did Jerusalem make from the gold and silver given by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Images of men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:17 says Jerusalem took the gold and silver given by the LORD and made images of men, committing whoredom with them.

questions.question: What did Jerusalem do with the fine flour, oil, and honey given to her as food?
options: Set it before idols for a sweet savour
questions.correctAnswer: Set it before idols for a sweet savour
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:19 explains that Jerusalem set the fine flour, oil, and honey before the idols for a sweet savour.

questions.question: True or False: Jerusalem sacrificed her own sons and daughters to idols to be devoured.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:20 states that Jerusalem took her sons and daughters and sacrificed them to idols to be devoured.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 16, what comes first?
options: The LORD washing Jerusalem with water
Jerusalem being cast out in the open field
Jerusalem entering into a covenant with the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem being cast out in the open field
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:5 describes Jerusalem being cast out on the day she was born before the LORD washes her (verse 9) or covers her with ornaments (verses 10-13) or enters into a covenant (verse 8).

questions.question: True or False: Jerusalem was swaddled and salted on the day of her birth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:4 specifically says Jerusalem was not salted nor swaddled at all on the day she was born.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 16:22, what had Jerusalem not remembered despite all her abominations and whoredoms?
options: The days of her youth when she was naked and bare
The covenant her God made with her
questions.correctAnswer: The days of her youth when she was naked and bare
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:22 clearly states Jerusalem did not remember the days of her youth when she was naked and bare and polluted in her blood, highlighting her forgetfulness of her humble beginnings despite her sins.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:24 say Jerusalem has built in every street?
options: An eminent place and a high place
Houses of worship for other gods
questions.correctAnswer: An eminent place and a high place
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:24 explains that Jerusalem built an eminent place and made a high place in every street, symbolizing idolatry and unfaithfulness.

questions.question: With whom did Jerusalem commit fornication, as mentioned in Ezekiel 16:26?
questions.correctAnswer: The Egyptians, her neighbours
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:26 states Jerusalem committed fornication with the Egyptians, her neighbours, increasing her whoredoms and provoking the Lord to anger.

questions.question: What consequence does Ezekiel 16:27 describe as a result of Jerusalem's actions?
options: God stretched out His hand and diminished her ordinary food
questions.correctAnswer: God stretched out His hand and diminished her ordinary food
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:27 explains that because of Jerusalem's sins, God stretched out His hand to diminish her ordinary food and delivered her to the will of those who hate her.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 16:28, Jerusalem was satisfied with her whoredoms with the Assyrians.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:28 states Jerusalem played the harlot with the Assyrians but could not be satisfied, indicating her insatiable sinful desires.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16:29 describe Jerusalem’s multiplication of fornication?
options: In the land of Canaan unto Chaldea, and still not satisfied
questions.correctAnswer: In the land of Canaan unto Chaldea, and still not satisfied
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:29 says Jerusalem multiplied fornication from Canaan to Chaldea and yet was not satisfied, emphasizing her relentless unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:30 say about Jerusalem’s heart?
options: It is weak because she continues in sin
questions.correctAnswer: It is weak because she continues in sin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:30 describes Jerusalem’s heart as weak because she continues the work of an imperious whorish woman, symbolizing her persistent rebellion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:31 say Jerusalem built at every head of the way?
questions.correctAnswer: Eminent places and high places
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:31 mentions that Jerusalem built eminent places and high places at every head of the way, indicating widespread idolatrous practices.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 16:32, Jerusalem is compared to what kind of woman?
options: A wife that commits adultery and takes strangers instead of her husband
questions.correctAnswer: A wife that commits adultery and takes strangers instead of her husband
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:32 compares Jerusalem to an adulterous wife who takes strangers instead of her husband, illustrating her spiritual unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What unique action did Jerusalem take compared to other women in her whoredoms, according to Ezekiel 16:34?
options: She gave gifts to her lovers but received no reward
She refused to give gifts to her lovers
She followed others in whoredoms without giving gifts
She was loyal to one lover
questions.correctAnswer: She gave gifts to her lovers but received no reward
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:34 explains Jerusalem gave gifts to all her lovers and hired them, but unlike others, she received no reward, making her contrary to other women.

questions.question: What is the reason for God's judgment on Jerusalem as stated in Ezekiel 16:36?
options: Because of her filthiness, nakedness, whoredoms, idols, and the blood of her children
Because she trusted in her beauty
questions.correctAnswer: Because of her filthiness, nakedness, whoredoms, idols, and the blood of her children
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:36 lists the reasons for judgment: filthiness poured out, nakedness discovered through whoredoms with idols, and the blood of her children given to them.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:38 say will happen to Jerusalem as a woman who breaks wedlock and sheds blood is judged?
options: She will be given blood in fury and jealousy
She will be exalted by the nations
She will be hidden from her lovers
questions.correctAnswer: She will be given blood in fury and jealousy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:38 declares Jerusalem will be judged like adulterous women who shed blood, receiving blood in fury and jealousy as a consequence.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 16:39, what will happen to Jerusalem's eminent places and high places?
options: They will be thrown down and broken
questions.correctAnswer: They will be thrown down and broken
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:39 states Jerusalem's eminent places and high places will be thrown down and broken by her enemies as part of the judgment.

questions.question: What final outcome does Ezekiel 16:42 promise after God's fury and jealousy depart from Jerusalem?
options: God will be quiet and no longer angry
questions.correctAnswer: God will be quiet and no longer angry
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:42 promises that after judgment, God's fury will rest, His jealousy will depart, and He will be quiet, indicating eventual peace.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16:23-24 connect Jerusalem’s wickedness to what she built in the city?
options: After all her wickedness, she built eminent places and high places in every street
Her wickedness caused her houses to be destroyed
Because of her wickedness, she was made queen of the nations
Her wickedness led her to build altars for the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: After all her wickedness, she built eminent places and high places in every street
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:23-24 connects Jerusalem’s wickedness with building eminent and high places, showing how her sin was expressed through idolatry in the city’s streets.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 16.

questions.question: What proverb is said against Jerusalem in Ezekiel 16, emphasizing the relation between mother and daughter?
options: As is the mother, so is her daughter
The apple does not fall far from the tree
questions.correctAnswer: As is the mother, so is her daughter
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:44 states the proverb used against Jerusalem is 'As is the mother, so is her daughter,' highlighting how Jerusalem's corruption follows from her origins.

questions.question: Who are identified as Jerusalem's 'elder sister' and 'younger sister' in Ezekiel 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Samaria and Sodom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:46 names Samaria as the elder sister and Sodom as the younger sister of Jerusalem, symbolizing their relationship and comparative sins.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 16, how does Jerusalem's corruption compare to that of Samaria and Sodom?
options: Jerusalem was more corrupt than both Samaria and Sodom
Jerusalem was less corrupt than both Samaria and Sodom
Jerusalem was equally corrupt as Samaria but less than Sodom
Jerusalem was equally corrupt as Sodom but less than Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem was more corrupt than both Samaria and Sodom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:47-48 explain that Jerusalem was corrupted more than her sisters Samaria and Sodom in all her ways.

questions.question: What sin is specifically mentioned as the iniquity of Sodom and her daughters in Ezekiel 16?
options: Pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness
questions.correctAnswer: Pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:49 details Sodom's sin as pride, fullness of bread, abundance of idleness, and neglecting the poor and needy.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare for Jerusalem's sins and for justifying her sisters' abominations?
options: Jerusalem will bear her own shame and be confounded
Jerusalem will be exalted above her sisters
Jerusalem will be forgiven without punishment
Jerusalem will lead her sisters in righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem will bear her own shame and be confounded
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:52 states that because Jerusalem judged her sisters but committed greater sins, she will bear her own shame and be confounded.

questions.question: What will happen when the captivity of Sodom, Samaria, and their daughters is brought back according to Ezekiel 16?
options: The captivity of Jerusalem and her daughters will also be brought back among them
Only Sodom and Samaria will be restored, not Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The captivity of Jerusalem and her daughters will also be brought back among them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:53 explains that when the captivity of Sodom and Samaria and their daughters is restored, Jerusalem's captivity will be restored in the midst of them.

questions.question: What is the ultimate purpose of God establishing an everlasting covenant with Jerusalem as stated in Ezekiel 16?
options: So that Jerusalem may know that He is the LORD
So that Jerusalem will never sin again
So that Jerusalem will become a nation of priests
So that Jerusalem will be free from all enemies
questions.correctAnswer: So that Jerusalem may know that He is the LORD
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:62 states God will establish His covenant with Jerusalem so she will know that He is the LORD.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 16 when describing Jerusalem’s relationship with God and her subsequent sins?
questions.correctAnswer: Extended allegory and apostrophe
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16 uses an extended allegory portraying Jerusalem as an unfaithful wife, and apostrophe as God addresses her directly, illustrating her spiritual adultery.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of covenant unfaithfulness and punishment similar to Ezekiel 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Hosea chapters 1-3
questions.explanation: Hosea 1-3 similarly portrays Israel as an unfaithful wife and discusses covenant unfaithfulness and restoration, paralleling Ezekiel 16's themes.

questions.question: What Hebrew term translated as 'whoredom' in Ezekiel 16 signifies spiritual unfaithfulness to God by idolatry?
questions.correctAnswer: Zonah
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Zonah' is used in Ezekiel 16 to describe 'whoredom,' symbolizing Israel's idolatry and covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16 depict God's initial act toward Jerusalem at her birth?
options: God passed by, saw her polluted in blood, and said 'Live!'
God immediately punished her for her abominations
God gave her riches and honor at birth
questions.correctAnswer: God passed by, saw her polluted in blood, and said 'Live!'
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:6 shows God noticing Jerusalem's vulnerable state at birth and commanding her to live, symbolizing divine mercy and election.

questions.question: What cultural context is essential to understand Jerusalem's 'making high places' and 'playing the harlot' in Ezekiel 16?
options: Ancient Near Eastern pagan worship often involved high places and ritual prostitution
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern pagan worship often involved high places and ritual prostitution
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:24-25 references 'high places' and 'harlotry,' reflecting pagan worship practices common in the ancient Near East involving sacred prostitution and idol worship.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 16, Jerusalem’s sins included sacrificing her own children to idols.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:20-21 explicitly state that Jerusalem sacrificed her sons and daughters to idols, evidencing her grave sins against God.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 16 promises that Jerusalem will never be restored or forgiven by God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:60-63 assures that God will remember His covenant and establish an everlasting covenant with Jerusalem, indicating restoration and forgiveness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of spiritual adultery and judgment found in Ezekiel 16?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 17
questions.explanation: Revelation 17 depicts the 'great whore' symbolizing spiritual unfaithfulness and judgment, paralleling themes from Ezekiel 16.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:3 reveal about Jerusalem's ancestry?
options: Jerusalem was born of a priest
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem's father was an Amorite
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:3 states, 'Thy father was an Amorite, and thy mother an Hittite,' highlighting Jerusalem's origins and its connection to the Canaanite nations.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 16:5, how is Jerusalem described at birth?
options: She was welcomed by her family
She was cast out in the open field
She was immediately given a name
questions.correctAnswer: She was cast out in the open field
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'but thou wast cast out in the open field,' illustrating the neglect and abandonment that characterized Jerusalem's early existence.

questions.question: What does the Lord declare to Jerusalem in Ezekiel 16:6?
options: To repent and turn back to Him
questions.correctAnswer: To live despite her state
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 16:6, God says, 'I said unto thee when thou wast in thy blood, Live,' showing His grace and desire for her survival despite her unclean state.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated in Ezekiel 16:8 when He enters into a covenant with Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:8 illustrates God's mercy as He covers Jerusalem's nakedness and establishes a covenant, demonstrating His grace despite her unworthiness.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:15 indicate about Jerusalem's attitude towards her beauty?
options: She trusted in her own beauty
She was humble about her appearance
questions.correctAnswer: She trusted in her own beauty
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But thou didst trust in thine own beauty,' indicating that Jerusalem became proud and self-reliant, leading to her downfall.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16:20 exemplify the severity of Jerusalem's actions?
options: She built temples to foreign gods
She engaged in trade with neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: She sacrificed her children
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:20 reveals the gravity of Jerusalem's sin as she 'hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured,' emphasizing her betrayal of God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'As is the mother, so is her daughter' in Ezekiel 16:44?
options: It emphasizes the continuity of sin
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the continuity of sin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:44 uses this phrase to highlight how Jerusalem mirrors the sins of her ancestors, indicating a persistent pattern of rebellion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:49 identify as the iniquity of Sodom?
questions.correctAnswer: Pride and idleness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:49 specifies, 'this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness,' illustrating the moral decay present in Sodom.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise in Ezekiel 16:60 despite Jerusalem's unfaithfulness?
options: To raise her above all nations
questions.correctAnswer: To remember His covenant
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:60 states, 'Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee,' showing God's faithfulness and the promise of restoration despite her sins.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 16:52 illustrate the concept of shame in God's judgment?
options: It shows God punishing the innocent
It indicates a reversal of status
It demonstrates the nature of divine love
questions.correctAnswer: It indicates a reversal of status
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:52 says, 'Thou also, which hast judged thy sisters, bear thine own shame for thy sins,' emphasizing the reversal of honor as Jerusalem is judged.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:57 say about Jerusalem's awareness of her wickedness?
options: She was unaware of her sins
She was proud of her actions
She was shamed by her actions
She blamed others for her sins
questions.correctAnswer: She was shamed by her actions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:57 indicates that Jerusalem's wickedness was discovered, leading to her shame, revealing the consequences of her actions.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:42 point to in terms of God's anger?
options: It is directed against the innocent
questions.correctAnswer: It will eventually rest
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:42 states, 'So will I make my fury toward thee to rest,' indicating that God's anger, while serious, has a purpose and will be resolved.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 16:30, how does God describe Jerusalem's actions?
questions.correctAnswer: As shameless
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:30 states, 'How weak is thine heart,' revealing God's disdain for Jerusalem's shameless actions and lack of repentance.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 16:53, what will happen to Jerusalem's captives?
options: They will be restored with her sisters
questions.correctAnswer: They will be restored with her sisters
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:53 promises, 'When I shall bring again their captivity,' indicating a future restoration of Jerusalem and her sisters, Sodom and Samaria.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 16:37 reveal about the consequences of Jerusalem's actions?
options: She will gain power over others
questions.correctAnswer: She will be judged publicly
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 16:37 states, 'I will gather all thy lovers... and will discover thy nakedness unto them,' indicating public judgment for her unfaithfulness.
